I am an old woman here in Kaskazini Pemba, and this small rice plot is what feeds my family. I do not have money to buy the chemical fertilizer from the shop, and I never went to school to learn about those things — I use the cow manure and chicken droppings I gather at home, like my mother taught me. The seed I keep from last harvest, because the improved seed costs too much and sometimes it does not like our land. For the water, the rains come and the low ground holds it for the rice, so I do not need to carry water; my daughter and I will do most of the work ourselves, but during transplanting and harvest I will call two neighbours and pay them with some of the rice.
